text:
## Executive summary

Sprint 43 finished above velocity but below scope. A day four customer escalation from Acme expanded the work in flight from 22 tickets to 28, and the team closed 22 of those for **73 story points** (versus a 60 SP baseline). Six tickets carry over, mostly small tasks and one in flight engineering blog post, none of them on the critical path.

## Highlights

- **Acme escalation resolved without an SLO breach.** Root cause investigation, hotfix on the API rate limit edge case, and a tenant level rate limit override all landed within four days of the customer report.
- **Bulk import retry storm fix** shipped along with a queue depth alert and a runbook so the incident does not recur silently.
- **Dashboard tab three (team usage heatmap) made GA** on schedule. Backend query, sortable team column, and the data caching all closed.
- **Login and sign up page redesigns shipped,** matching the Sprint 42 hero pattern.

## Watch list

- Six tickets carry over to Sprint 44, including the daily digest A B test setup and two P2 backlog sweeps. Worth pulling these into Sprint 44 day one so they do not slip again.
- The auth migration staging dry run is in review, the rollback runbook is still in to do. Sprint 44 hinges on landing both before the production cutover attempt.
- Engineering blog post for the new auth flow is unassigned in to do. If we want the cutover story externalized, this needs an owner by Sprint 44 day three.

## Recommendations

- Ask leadership to commit to a scope freeze 48 hours before sprint review for sprints where customer escalations land mid sprint. This sprint absorbed 25 story points of new work and still hit velocity, but the carryover signals the team paid a focus cost.
- Run a 30 minute post mortem on the Acme escalation in the Sprint 44 retro slot. Capture what the customer signal looked like at day minus seven so we can build an earlier detection path.
- Pair Priya Sharma with Alex Chen on the auth migration runbook review before the Sprint 44 cutover. The two seniors carried the escalation, both have full context, and the rollback path benefits from a second set of eyes.

## Talking points

- **Customer escalation absorbed without SLO breach.** Root cause, hotfix, and tenant level guard rail all shipped inside four days.
- **Velocity beat baseline at 73 story points** versus a 60 SP baseline, even after 25 SP of unplanned scope landed mid sprint.
- **Six carryover tickets** are mostly P2 tasks plus one in flight engineering blog post. No critical path slippage.
- **Auth migration on plan for Sprint 44.** Staging dry run in review, production cutover scheduled.
- **Recommend a 48 hour scope freeze rule** for sprints that absorb customer escalations.

metadata.notes: Hand curated. References sprint 43 fixture values verbatim (scope 22 to 28, velocity 73 SP, baseline 60 SP, six carryovers, mid sprint escalation Acme). Tone neutral about the scope creep so the brief still reads as celebratory of the velocity beat.
